Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: B
Q2: A
Q3: REFRAME
Q4: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: B works the same way as the sync's existing additive step for `.gitattributes` (`.github/workflows/update_workflows.yml`, step "Sync changelog fragment assets from upstream", lines 799-836), which keeps the consumer's own settings. One part of B is narrowed: the sync must not add a `github-actions` entry the consumer doesn't have. Without that entry Dependabot opens no version-bump PRs for these files, and adding one would start version updates the consumer never asked for. The execution plan below makes this binding.
Q2: The integrity check sets the managed set in `.github/workflows/workflow_integrity.yml` `compare()` (lines 276-306). It is the `WORKFLOW_PROFILE` profile entries, plus the integrity wrapper (`INTEGRITY_WRAPPER`, line 282), plus `ai-update-workflows.yml` (`UPDATER_WRAPPER`, line 173) when that file exists. Excluding exactly that set stops the failing PRs, and the consumer's own workflows still get bumps. Dependabot's `exclude-paths` accepts glob or literal file paths relative to the update directory (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference, https://github.blog/changelog/2025-08-26-dependabot-can-now-exclude-automatic-pull-requests-for-manifests-in-selected-subdirectories/).
Q3: Option A cannot be done as written. `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` (lines 89, 127, 167) pins `actions/checkout` by commit SHA (`fbc6f399... # v5.1.0`). No v6 or v7 checkout SHA appears anywhere in the repo, and the implementer has no network access, so writing a v7.0.1 SHA would mean inventing one. Option B only partly holds up: GitHub's docs say Dependabot with `directory: "/"` scans `.github/workflows/` and a root `action.yml` only, not plain `workflow-templates/*.yml` (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/secure-your-dependencies/auto-update-actions). So the decision is to ship B limited to what the docs support, and not to bump any SHA by hand.
Q4: A is the most conservative choice. GitHub facts show the example PR shubhodeep1/mongo-explorer#68 is already closed and not merged. Option B would give the sync a new power (closing PRs) that the issue doesn't need once new bump PRs stop.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml (the additive step "Sync changelog fragment assets from upstream", lines 799-836, gated by `inputs.allow_workflow_edits != false`; the profile/manifest loop at lines 955-983)
    - scripts/build_sync_manifest.py (`derive_allowed_paths`, the `allowed_consumer_paths` payload at line 422)
    - .github/workflows/workflow_integrity.yml (the inline staged-path policy around lines 428-498)
  steps:
    - Add a new additive sync step to `update_workflows.yml`, gated like `changelog_sync`. It runs an upstream helper from the `@stable` support checkout, the same way `assemble_changelog.py ensure-assets` is run, and records changed paths in a changed-paths file.
    - The helper reads `.github/dependabot.yml`, or `.github/dependabot.yaml` if that is the one present. It is a no-op with a log line in each of these cases: no file, no `package-ecosystem: github-actions` entry, or no entry whose `directory`/`directories` covers `/`. It never creates the file or the entry.
    - For each matching `github-actions` entry, it sets `exclude-paths` to the consumer's own entries plus the sync-owned entries from Q2. It treats any `.github/workflows/<name>` entry whose `<name>` is a basename in upstream `workflow-templates/*.yml` as sync-owned. Those entries are replaced on each run, so the list follows profile changes. All other keys and entries are kept.
    - If the file doesn't parse as YAML, the helper leaves it untouched, logs a warning, and fails open (the sync continues).
    - Make sure the signed sync manifest's `allowed_consumer_paths` (`scripts/build_sync_manifest.py`) and the staged-path policies in `update_workflows.yml` and `workflow_integrity.yml` allow `.github/dependabot.yml` / `.github/dependabot.yaml`, so the staged change passes PR-delivery verification.
    - Add contract tests covering: no file, no `github-actions` entry, existing consumer `exclude-paths` kept, sync-owned entries replaced after a profile change, invalid YAML left untouched, and the manifest allow-list includes the path.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: Option B's "or add that entry if missing"
  equivalence_argument: Without a `github-actions` entry, Dependabot opens no version-bump PRs against the wrappers, so there is nothing to exclude. Not adding the entry keeps the consumer's settings exactly as they are.
  reversibility: The helper owns only `.github/workflows/<template>` entries. Removing the step stops future edits, and the consumer can delete the sync-owned entries by hand.
Q3:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - workflow-templates/ai-review.yml lines 89, 127, 167 (`actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09  # v5.1.0`)
    - .github/workflows/*.yml (139 `actions/checkout@` uses across 44 files)
  steps:
    - Add `.github/dependabot.yml` to coding-workflows with one update entry: `package-ecosystem: "github-actions"`, `directory: "/"`, a weekly schedule. Do not list `/workflow-templates`, because the docs don't promise Dependabot scans plain workflow files there.
    - Leave the pins in `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` unchanged. Do not write any new action SHA that isn't already in the checkout.
    - Add a contract test that parses the new upstream `dependabot.yml` and checks it has the `github-actions` entry with `directory: "/"`.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "one-time bump of `actions/checkout` in `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` to v7.0.1" (from Q3:A)
  equivalence_argument: Bumps upstream now come from Dependabot, which writes the real commit SHAs. Once a bumped pin has merged upstream, a later change can copy it into `workflow-templates/` without guessing. Inventing a SHA is not allowed, and a wrong pin would break every consumer's review workflow.
  reversibility: Deleting `.github/dependabot.yml` undoes the change. The template bump can be done in a later issue once a verified v7.x SHA is in the repo.
